anti_goals: Do not implement preset field validation, defaults, labels, colors or Settings configuration owned by FT-005.
Do not implement overdue fullscreen rendering, alert sound selection/ramp/cap or silent/DND presentation owned by FT-007/FT-009.
Do not implement API-key, location, alert-volume or glass-personalization settings from FT-008/FT-009.
Do not add reboot auto-start/recovery, a new module, dependency, event/message boundary, backend, cloud sync, accounts, Google Services or unaccepted UI controls.
constraints: Timer & Alert is the sole owner of active-timer persistence, elapsed arithmetic and idle|countdown|overdue transitions; consumers use its public projection and commands.
Main Display owns presentation and gesture dispatch through the accepted Main Display -> Timer & Alert contract; it must not calculate remaining time or read Timer & Alert private storage.
Settings & Location remains the owner of validated preset configuration; Timer & Alert reads the FT-005 projection and does not write settings or duplicate validation rules.
Android Runtime Adapter owns device/lifecycle/network signals and audio policy; the composition root forwards signals and wires capabilities but owns no timer business state.
Use the accepted persisted start point and positive configured duration for rehydration. Reboot recovery is explicitly excluded, and overdue presentation/audio remains downstream.
evidence_required: [FT-006-AC-001; REQ-012] Expected RED: the Foundation surface has no accepted user-facing short-tap countdown projection. GREEN: a valid selected preset starts immediately, countdown replaces the large clock, current time moves aside and the originating button is highlighted. Compare each start/projection condition; mandatory artifact is the deterministic start/integration result, while scoped device observation is deferred/non-blocking where host proof is insufficient.

[FT-006-AC-002; REQ-011] Expected RED: the Foundation/FT-005 seam has no accepted runtime proof that starting a configured preset preserves one active timer. GREEN: the Timer & Alert owner exposes at most one active timer while consuming the validated preset projection and never creates parallel active records. Compare active-state cardinality and ownership; artifact is the isolated Timer & Alert/Settings integration result.

[FT-006-AC-003; REQ-013] Expected RED: a countdown has no accepted protected-cancellation gesture path. GREEN: single tap leaves countdown active and shows the accepted hint; double tap anywhere cancels and returns to the standard display. Compare both gesture transitions and the final idle state; artifact is the deterministic gesture result.

[FT-006-AC-004; REQ-014] Expected RED: the current timer surface does not prove rehydration across accepted temporary interruptions. GREEN: after Activity/foreground/screen-off/temporary process interruption, persisted start/duration data recalculates the correct remaining countdown or overdue lifecycle state; no reboot recovery is claimed. Compare elapsed/remaining/state at synthetic timestamps and the accepted host route; artifact is the mandatory isolated persistence/rehydration result plus deferred/non-blocking target-ROM evidence where host proof is insufficient.

[FT-006-AC-005; REQ-025] Expected RED: the current product path has no feature-level proof that network/weather-service loss leaves timer operations usable, including dismissal of an already-overdue state. GREEN: with network/provider availability absent, start and countdown remain functional, protected cancellation remains available, and an already-overdue timer is dismissed by any tap and returns to Main Display. Compare each accepted transition with no provider input; artifact is the deterministic offline/no-provider lifecycle result. Do not claim FT-007 overdue rendering or audio behavior.

success_outcome: A clean Android build and deterministic redacted evidence prove that a validated selected preset starts immediately, only one timer is active, single-tap countdown cancellation is protected while double tap cancels, persisted start/duration data restores the correct countdown or overdue lifecycle state after temporary interruption, and with network/provider input absent an already-overdue timer is dismissed by any tap back to Main Display while accepted capability ownership and scope remain intact.
title: Implement countdown lifecycle, protected cancellation and temporary recovery
verification_targets: FT-006-AC-001 / REQ-012: a valid selected preset starts immediately; countdown replaces the large clock, current time moves aside and the originating button is highlighted.
FT-006-AC-002 / REQ-011: Timer & Alert consumes the validated FT-005 preset projection and maintains at most one active timer without parallel active records or a second state owner.

FT-006-AC-004 / REQ-014: Activity/foreground/screen-off/temporary process interruption rehydrates from persisted start/duration data and recalculates the correct countdown or overdue lifecycle state; reboot recovery is excluded.
